Inherited intestinal glucose-galactose transport failure causes severe malabsorption; renal insufficiency and stones occur in fewer than 30%.
Retinal dysplasia and persistent hyaloid vascular remnants establish an ocular developmental disorder.
Follicular ichthyosis, atrichia and ocular photophobia define IFAP; ectrodactyly occurs in 4/13 (~31%). Other BRESHECK organ defects are individually below 30%.
Inherited erythrokeratoderma with plaques and erythema in 8/8 patients; no established other-organ damage.
Benign tumour originating in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes.

Anterior pituitary hormone hypersecretion defines the umbrella; other-organ effects vary substantially by hormonal subtype.
Hereditary bipolar/affective disorder; psychiatric phenotype does not establish neurologic organ damage.

Mature B-cell lymphoma qualifies as both a blood-cell neoplasm and lymphoma mechanism; no specific extranodal organ is defining.
Inherited D-lactate metabolism disorder; neurologic and ocular findings lack established >=30% frequency. Gout susceptibility is a risk, not direct involvement.
Disorder of neurologic circadian sleep-wake regulation; no established direct damage to other organs.
Familial CARD14-associated inflammatory keratinization disorder affects skin and nails; ocular and oral abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
